SQL_INJECTION.title: SQL Injection Detected
SQL_INJECTION.remediation: Never build SQL from user input. Use prepared statements / parameterised queries so the driver separates code from data, and validate input against an allow-list.

code.java:
PreparedStatement ps = conn.prepareStatement("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?");
ps.setInt(1, id);
code.go: row := db.QueryRowContext(ctx, "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?", id)

COMMAND_INJECTION.title: OS Command Injection
COMMAND_INJECTION.remediation: Do not pass untrusted data to a shell. Call the binary directly with an argument list (no shell), keep shell=False, and allow-list the permitted commands.

code.javascript:
const { execFile } = require('child_process');
execFile('/bin/ls', ['-l', path], cb);
code.default: run the binary directly with an argument vector, never through a shell

CODE_INJECTION.title: Dynamic Code Evaluation
CODE_INJECTION.remediation: Remove dynamic code execution. Replace eval/exec with an explicit dispatch table (dict of allowed operations) and render templates from files, never from user strings.

code.javascript:
const handlers = { sum: (a) => a.reduce((x, y) => x + y, 0) };
handlers[op](data);
code.default: use a dispatch table instead of evaluating strings as code

XSS.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
XSS.remediation: Escape/encode every untrusted value in its output context (HTML, attribute, JS, URL) and prefer framework templates that auto-escape. Use a strict Content-Security-Policy as defence in depth.

code.javascript:
element.textContent = userInput;              // preferred
el.innerHTML = he.encode(userInput);        // if HTML is required
code.default: encode untrusted output for its context before rendering

PATH_TRAVERSAL.title: Path Traversal / Local File Inclusion
PATH_TRAVERSAL.remediation: Resolve the path against a fixed base directory and reject anything that escapes it. Allow-list file names instead of accepting raw paths, and never concatenate user input into a filesystem path.

code.php:
$target = realpath(BASE_DIR . '/' . basename($name));
if ($target === false || !str_starts_with($target, BASE_DIR)) { exit; }
code.javascript:
const target = path.resolve(UPLOAD_DIR, path.basename(name));
if (!target.startsWith(UPLOAD_DIR)) throw new Error('illegal path');
code.default: resolve against a trusted base directory and verify containment

DESERIALIZATION.title: Unsafe Deserialization
DESERIALIZATION.remediation: Never deserialize untrusted data with a format that can execute code. Use JSON (or another data-only format), schema validation, and for YAML always pass Loader=SafeLoader.

code.python:
import yaml
data = yaml.load(text, Loader=yaml.SafeLoader)

# pickle: use json instead of pickle.loads()
code.javascript: const data = JSON.parse(text);   // never unserialize user blobs
code.default: use a data-only format such as JSON with schema validation

WEAK_CRYPTO.title: Weak Cryptography
WEAK_CRYPTO.remediation: MD5/SHA-1 and non-CSPRNG generators must not protect secrets. Use SHA-256+ (or bcrypt/scrypt/argon2 for passwords) and a cryptographically secure RNG.

code.python:
import hashlib, secrets
fingerprint = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
token = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
code.javascript:
const fingerprint = await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', buf);
const token = crypto.randomUUID();

HARDCODED_SECRET.title: Hardcoded Credential or Secret
HARDCODED_SECRET.remediation: Remove the literal from source, rotate the exposed value, and read it at runtime from an environment variable or a secret manager. Keep a .env file out of version control.

SSRF.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
SSRF.remediation: Do not let users choose the destination URL. Allow-list schemes and hosts, block private/link-local ranges (127.0.0.0/8, 10.0.0.0/8, 169.254.0.0/16, metadata IPs) and resolve the DNS before connecting.

code.javascript:
const u = new URL(url);
if (!ALLOWED_HOSTS.includes(u.hostname)) throw new Error('blocked host');
code.default: validate the destination against an allow-list before requesting it

INSECURE_CONFIG.title: Insecure Configuration
INSECURE_CONFIG.remediation: Turn debug mode off in production, restrict CORS to known origins, pin ALLOWED_HOSTS, and never disable CSRF protection globally.

code.default: deny by default; enable only what production needs

VULNERABLE_DEPENDENCY.title: Vulnerable Dependency
VULNERABLE_DEPENDENCY.remediation: Upgrade to the patched version listed in the advisory, then re-scan. Pin exact versions and run an SCA check in CI so regressions are caught before release.

code.default: pip install --upgrade <package>   # or npm audit fix / composer update

TAINT_FLOW.title: Untrusted Data Reaches a Dangerous Sink
TAINT_FLOW.remediation: Sanitise or validate the value where it enters the system, then use the safe API for the sink (parameterised query, argument vector, auto-escaping template). See the specific sink rule for the exact fix.

code.default: value = sanitize(value)   # trusted input only, then call the safe API

DANGEROUS_SINK.title: Dangerous Function Used
DANGEROUS_SINK.remediation: Prefer the safe equivalent of this API and only call it with trusted, validated input. If the call is unavoidable, allow-list the arguments and fail closed.

code.default: use the safe API variant with validated input

GENERIC.title: Security Finding
GENERIC.remediation: Review the flagged code, confirm whether untrusted input can reach it, and apply the framework-recommended safe API for this operation.
